premiums.name: MJP Q4 (Main Japanese Port)
premiums.src: COMPILED MONDAY 26-OCTOBER-2026 (BEFORE THE RING; LATEST PUBLISHED OFFICIAL) (LME BOARD ON THE FRIDAY 23-OCTOBER OFFICIAL). PREMIUM ASSESSMENTS ARE PERIODIC, NOT DAILY, AND THIS PANEL CARRIES EACH ROW AT ITS OWN LAST PUBLIC ASSESSMENT DATE. CIF JAPAN SPOT REFRESHED THIS RUN TO SMM'S 09-OCTOBER ASSESSMENT: CIF Japan MJP spot $230/t (warehouse-warrant $269/t; FCA South Korea $223/t, CIF South Korea $216/t, CIF Thailand P1020A $249/t), down from the $370/t last public spot carried since Q3. SMM's read is that overseas premiums are 'near a floor' with the outlook 'less bearish', though a stronger rebound needs better downstream orders. The prior $370/t mark and the new $230/t mark are not guaranteed to share one assessor, so the size of the step is indicative. EVERY OTHER ROW IS CARRIED UNCHANGED at its own last public assessment. SMM also cites the US Midwest duty-paid premium at 105 US cents/lb (about $2,315/t) on 09-October - context from a different source, not substituted into the US rows. CONTEXT FROM A DIFFERENT ASSESSOR, NOT MIXED INTO ANY ROW: AL Circle (06-October) reports CRU's Asia CIF premium at $202/t and Q4 MJP offers down to $245-260/t from $325/t in early September, against the $395/t Q3 benchmark; earlier SMM reporting (30-September) had Rio Tinto at $280/t and South32 at $265/t. Q4 SETTLEMENT NOW PUBLIC: Reuters (07-October) reported that some Japanese buyers agreed Q4 premiums of $255/t with global producers including Rio Tinto and South32, down 35% from $395/t in Q3 and below initial offers of $310-325/t; talks with other buyers were ongoing. This page first recorded it on 11-October. THE TARIFF DECOMPOSITION IS REFRESHED DAILY BY DESIGN: on a re-verified Section 232 rate of 50% on aluminium articles applied to full customs value, the tariff leg of the US duty-paid premium is 0.50 times the 23-October official cash of $3,043.00, or $1,521.50, UP $5.00 on the day. Against a US Midwest duty-paid premium of $2,403/t that leaves a residual market leg of $881.50, so 63.3% of the US duty-paid premium is policy arithmetic rather than market. This page does NOT fabricate freight, financing or tightness splits for any premium row. SOURCE DISAGREEMENT FLAGGED 17-OCTOBER: SMM's 16-October overseas-market analysis describes Q4 MJP negotiations as slow, with the two sides 'diverging significantly' on price; this is consistent with Reuters' 07-October report that $255/t was agreed with SOME buyers while talks with others continued. The $255/t settlement is retained; no new figure was located. Source: https://news.metal.com/newscontent/104162844-smm-analysis-overseas-primary-aluminum-market-remains-weak-offer-prices-under-pressure-across-major-markets

CHINESE CUSTOMS DATA PUBLISHED FRIDAY CUT THE EX-CHINA PULL ARGUMENT FROM BOTH ENDS, AND IT IS THE MOST SUBSTANTIVE NEW FUNDAMENTAL INFORMATION IN THIS WINDOW. August primary aluminium imports fell 14.65% year on year to 185,500 tonnes, with Russia supplying 96% of them; January-August imports were 1.66 million tonnes, down 3.41%. On the same day, August aluminium extrusion exports printed a 2026 high of 92,500 tonnes, up 9.7% year on year, with September guided lower at 85,000-92,000 tonnes on a narrowing China-to-overseas price spread. Less Chinese buying of ex-China primary and more Chinese semis in third markets both work against the ex-China tightness case, whatever the stated structural cause.

THE RATE PATH WORSENED AGAIN AND THE WHOLE LME COMPLEX FELT IT. The US ten-year is near 5.24%, close to its highest since 2002, with roughly 70% market-implied odds of an October Fed hike; the dollar index is near 101.28 and the LME euro fixing fell to 1.1375 from 1.1403. Copper fell 1.33% and zinc 2.54% on cash on 28-September; aluminium's front tightened regardless.

THE ENERGY AND CURRENCY LEGS BOTH EASED. European gas TTF fell 4.02% to EUR 71.93/MWh, the largest single-session fall of this window and a direct improvement in the economics of the European smelting capacity currently guided to restart; Brent slipped 0.56% to $106.01; the dollar index fell 0.32% to 100.966 and the LME euro fixing rose 0.30% to 1.14030, ending two sessions of dollar strength. Cheaper European power is bearish for price through supply and supportive for European converter margins - the two effects are opposite and are stated separately rather than netted.

alumina_notes: THE ALUMINA PANEL REFRESHED PROPERLY THIS RUN FOR THE FIRST TIME IN A MONTH, AND THE MESSAGE IS QUIET-BUT-SOFTENING. SMM's 24-September weekly index prints at 2,671.59 yuan/tonne, down 2.35 yuan/tonne or 0.09% week on week, with all five regional quotes flat week on week - Shandong 2,640-2,710, Henan 2,680-2,740, Shanxi 2,670-2,730, Guangxi 2,580-2,630, Guizhou 2,720-2,780. This replaces a 25-August mark of 2,600 yuan/tonne that this page had been carrying for a month, and the difference between the two is a month of drift, not a session's move. PUBLISHED ON THE SAME DAY: China's weekly alumina operating rate rose 0.23 percentage points to 76.89%, on 119.62 million tonnes a year of installed metallurgical-grade capacity and 91.97 million tonnes of operating capacity. MORE ALUMINA BEING MADE AT A PRICE THAT IS NOT MOVING IS A SOFT SIGNAL FOR ALUMINA AND THEREFORE A SUPPORTIVE ONE FOR SMELTER MARGINS, SINCE ALUMINA IS ROUGHLY A THIRD OF A SMELTER'S CASH COST AND IT TAKES ABOUT TWO TONNES OF IT TO MAKE ONE TONNE OF METAL. It is also a reminder that the cost-side relief on this page is coming from alumina while the cost-side pressure is coming from energy, which rose again today. The dollar-denominated rows - FOB East Australia, the exchange-settled alumina close and the futures reference - carry no newer dated print into this window and are held at their true assessment dates. The freshest hard FOB East Australia datum remains the 18-September SMM-reported trade at $354/mt for October shipment.

news.headline: CHINA DESTOCKING CONTINUES, EX-CHINA SUPPLY CAPS UPSIDE (SMM morning summary, 26-October): Chinese aluminium ingot social inventory fell 30,000 t from last Thursday and 54,000 t from last Monday. In Friday's session the most-traded SHFE contract closed at RMB 23,575/t (+RMB 225, +0.96%) and LME three-month closed electronic trade at $3,040.5/t (+$34.5, +1.15%); East China spot premiums were RMB 240-260/t. SMM describes ex-China premiums as generally weak and expects prices to consolidate, with ex-China restarts and new capacity weighing against Chinese destocking. READ: physical China is tight; the ceiling comes from Gulf and other ex-China supply returning.

THREE-REGION INGOT STOCKS FALL AGAIN (SMM, 26-October): aluminium ingot inventory across three major Chinese consumption hubs stood in the 410,000-tonne range, a tenth straight working-day decline with all three regions destocking. READ: the post-holiday draw is extending into late October, supporting Shanghai prices and import arbitrage interest.

HORMUZ STILL EFFECTIVELY CLOSED (Straits Daily Brief, 26-October): the brief describes the strait as effectively closed to commercial traffic, with 4 transits recorded on 18-October (IMF PortWatch) against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 a day and 118 vessels holding position in the Gulf watch box. Brent was $115.43 at 00:08 UTC, down 1.11% over 24 hours. Iranian state media denies making new reopening proposals via Pakistan; reports of an Iranian reopening offer and of mine-free routes are single-source and unverified. READ: Gulf metal and raw-material flows stay exposed; energy-cost support for prices persists.

RUSSIA: SECOND SELLER OF PRIMARY METAL (AL Circle, 24-October): Sual Partners signed a production-sharing agreement with state-controlled RusHydro giving it access to up to 150,000 t of aluminium (up to half the output) from the Boguchany smelter in Siberia, with supply of alumina, anodes, aluminium fluoride and silicon also covered. Announced 15-October during Russian Energy Week. READ: no change to total Russian supply; a marketing shift worth watching for Russian metal flows. The article does not confirm sales have started.

OVERNIGHT: BASE METALS RISE, CRUDE SURGES (SMM, published 25-October): in Friday's overnight session LME aluminium rose 1.03% and the most-traded SHFE aluminium contract 1.62%, with cast aluminium +1.74% and alumina futures -0.51%. Brent rose 3.72% overnight and 6.85% on the week (a fourth straight weekly gain), WTI 3.99%, on Houthi attacks on Saudi oil facilities, a drone strike on Aramco's Shaybah field, an IRGC statement that Hormuz shipping had stopped and reports of two supertankers striking mines; a reported G7 strategic-reserve release did not stop the rally. Markets expect US rates higher for longer into the 28-October FOMC; University of Michigan sentiment fell to 48.0. READ: post-official moves point to a firmer Monday open, but the board stays on Friday's official.

READ: ex-China alumina keeps softening, which eases smelter raw-material cost even as energy costs rise. Origin-specific trade cited as context only; not substituted into the alumina rows.

CHINA: FASTEST POST-HOLIDAY DESTOCK IN SIX YEARS (SMM, 22-October): aluminium ingot social inventory fell 53,000 t in the second week after National Day, after 50,000 t the week before - 103,000 t over two weeks, and SMM says the single-week fall is the largest for the period since 2020. Billet stocks fell 20,000 t (39,000 t over two weeks). During the holiday ingots had built only 48,000 t. READ: Chinese physical offtake is firmer than prices suggest.

ENERGY HOLDS HIGH (Trading Economics, 22-October): Brent near $110.30 (+1.4%) after Trading Economics reported a drone attack on Saudi Aramco's Shaybah field and a US order for some embassy staff to leave Saudi Arabia; Middle East export flows are nearing pre-war levels. EU TTF gas was about EUR 87.3/MWh with storage 74.58% full on 21-October, the lowest seasonal level since records began in 2009. READ: European and Gulf smelter energy costs stay elevated.

earnings.headline: BACKFILLED INTO THIS PANEL THIS RUN WITH A FULL FOUR-QUARTER SOURCED HISTORY. Constellium reported Q2-2026 Adjusted EBITDA of $439 MILLION, a record, taking H1-2026 to $798m, and RAISED FULL-YEAR 2026 GUIDANCE to $980m-$1.020bn of Adjusted EBITDA EXCLUDING METAL PRICE LAG with free cash flow in excess of $300m. Leverage was 1.8x at the quarter end. Management states that the 2028 targets of $900m ex-lag EBITDA and $300m of free cash flow will now be met two years early. THE METAL PRICE LAG IS THE NUMBER THAT MATTERS FOR READING THIS PAGE and it is disclosed by the company: the $439m headline INCLUDES a $129m non-cash benefit from metal price lag, so the ex-lag figure is $310m. The four-quarter ex-lag path is $196m, $213m, $262m, $310m against headline figures of $235m, $280m, $359m and $439m - the gap between the two series has widened every quarter.
earnings.readthrough: THE READ-THROUGH IS THE MOST IMPORTANT ONE ON THIS PANEL FOR ANYONE TRYING TO SIZE HOW MUCH OF THE 2026 EARNINGS CYCLE IS REAL. Constellium is a converter, not a smelter: it buys primary and scrap and sells rolled and extruded product, so a rising LME shows up in its results as a NON-CASH metal price lag benefit before it shows up anywhere in the operating business. That lag contributed $126m across the whole of FY2025 and $226m in the FIRST HALF of 2026 alone - it has nearly doubled in half the time. UNDERLYING PERFORMANCE IS GENUINELY GOOD, with ex-lag Adjusted EBITDA up 58% from $196m in Q3-2025 to $310m in Q2-2026 and the company pulling its 2028 targets forward by two years - but a reader who takes the $439m headline as operating performance overstates it by 29%. THE GENERAL POINT EXTENDS ACROSS THIS WHOLE PANEL: a large share of the 2026 aluminium earnings recovery is price-lag and inventory revaluation rather than volume or spread, which is exactly the kind of earnings that reverses when the LME stops rising - and the completed August board, on which aluminium's monthly mean rose 2.97% against copper's 6.12% and zinc's 7.76%, is the first evidence that it may be about to.

The company reported its highest-ever Q1 bauxite excavation at 19.52 lakh tonnes and its highest-ever Q1 calcined alumina production at 5.77 lakh tonnes. Added to this board and to the earnings-history panel this run as the designated progressive backfill.
earnings.readthrough: NALCO IS THE MOST FULLY INTEGRATED PRODUCER ON THIS PANEL - IT MINES ITS OWN BAUXITE, REFINES ITS OWN ALUMINA AND SMELTS - AND THAT IS EXACTLY WHY THIS PRINT IS USEFUL RATHER THAN JUST GOOD. A company that buys none of its alumina nearly doubling profit on record volumes tells you where margin is sitting in the chain: with whoever owns the alumina. Read directly against Chalco, the largest alumina producer in the world, whose Q2-2026 attributable profit fell 26.2% year on year in a quarter when the LME cash average was above $3,200 - the difference between the two is not the metal price, which both received, but scale, cost position and product mix. IT ALSO CUTS AGAINST THE ALUMINA-COST-SHOCK RISK THIS BOARD CARRIES: an integrated refiner posting record Q1 alumina output at 5.77 lakh tonnes is evidence of alumina availability rather than scarcity, and it sits on the same side of the argument as the alumina-to-aluminium ratio near 10.7-11.3%, well below the historical norm. THE HONEST QUALIFICATION: NALCO's exposure is predominantly Indian and its cost base is domestic coal-fired, so it is a weak read on seaborne alumina tightness, which is where this board locates the risk. Public listed-company disclosure, carried to read the cycle only.

earnings.readthrough: THE WORLD'S LARGEST ALUMINA PRODUCER EARNED MATERIALLY LESS IN A QUARTER WHEN THE LME CASH AVERAGE WAS ABOVE $3,200, AND THAT IS THE SIGNAL. A 26% year-on-year fall in Q2 attributable profit on flat-to-lower revenue points to margin compression rather than volume weakness, and it is consistent with the Chinese alumina spot picture carried on this board - SMM's Shandong index down toward 2,600 RMB/t with national capacity utilisation rising and trader inventories building. For a reader of the seaborne market the implication runs both ways: weaker Chinese alumina margins are disinflationary for the smelter cost basket globally, but a large integrated producer earning less at a high metal price also argues that the cost curve has moved up underneath everyone. The shares fell around 3% on the release. NOTE: the reported H1 attributable profit of RMB 7.071bn does not reconcile with the sum of the reported Q1 and Q2 quarterly figures, and that discrepancy is disclosed on the earnings-history panel rather than resolved by inference.

earnings.headline: STRONGEST QUARTER OF THE YEAR AT THE DOWNSTREAM END OF THE CHAIN. Fourth-quarter FY26 revenue rose 25.2% year-on-year to MYR 204.8 million (USD 50.8 million) from MYR 163.5 million (USD 40.5 million), on higher sales volumes in the group's extrusion and fabrication segment; the company reports its strongest quarterly revenue and profit of the financial year, with the headline putting quarterly profit up about 200% to roughly USD 4.5 million. The result funds a MYR 100 million (USD 24.8 million) expansion plan and a diversification away from its core solar-sector business. FIGURES ARE TAKEN FROM THE PUBLIC REPORT AS PUBLISHED; the full profit-and-loss detail below the revenue line was truncated in the public summary and nothing is inferred to fill it.
earnings.readthrough: A USEFUL COUNTERWEIGHT TO THE CHINESE DOWNSTREAM PICTURE RATHER THAN A CONTRADICTION OF IT, AND THE DISTINCTION IS GEOGRAPHIC. SMM's 24-August daily describes Chinese downstream processing operating rates as under pressure with pre-peak-season stockpiling absent, and Chinese billet inventory is at a five-year seasonal high. A South-East Asian extruder posting 25% revenue growth and its best quarter of the year says the weakness is not uniform across Asia - which is consistent with the trade-flow story on this board, where South-East Asia is being consolidated as the major supplementary scrap source by the UAE export ban and EU tariff increase. IT IS A SMALL COMPANY AND ONE QUARTER, SO IT IS WEIGHTED ACCORDINGLY: it is evidence that extrusion demand outside China is holding, not evidence that the global peak season has arrived.

earnings.headline: H1-2026 interim results: alumina sales volume 1.296 Mt (+15.0% y/y from ~1.127 Mt) but average realised selling price USD 320/t against USD 529/t (-39.5%); revenue USD 415.0m (-30.5% y/y from USD 596.8m); gross profit USD 65.5m from USD 303.9m; gross margin 15.8% from 50.9%; profit attributable USD 62.7m (-74.8%); basic EPS USD 0.10 from USD 0.46; interim dividend cut to HKD 0.16 from HKD 0.65. Cash and equivalents more than doubled to USD 666.7m with no borrowings; total assets USD 2.496bn (+11.0%).
earnings.readthrough: THE VALUE OF THIS DISCLOSURE IS THAT IT IS A REALISED PRICE ACROSS 1.3 MILLION TONNES, NOT AN ASSESSMENT - which makes it the single best public measurement of how far alumina has actually fallen. A 39.5% decline in realised ASP to USD 320/t, against a company-stated average international alumina price of about USD 307/t on an LME Platts basis versus about USD 447/t a year earlier, confirms from the seller's own accounts that the 2024-25 alumina squeeze has fully unwound. FOR THE METAL THIS IS MARGIN-POSITIVE AND PRICE-NEGATIVE, AND BOTH LEGS DESERVE EQUAL BILLING: non-integrated smelters buy alumina cheaper, but a lower cost curve lowers the price at which supply discipline would ever appear. THE SECOND-ORDER POINT IS THE CAPITAL: cash more than doubled to USD 666.7m with no borrowings, funding preparatory work on a 250,000 t/y Indonesian electrolytic aluminium first phase at about USD 436.6m over roughly two years with a further 500,000 t/y flagged medium term. Weak alumina prices are not slowing the ex-China metal capacity pipeline - they are being converted into it. Public disclosure only; no company-specific or confidential information is used or implied.

earnings.headline: H1-2026 unaudited interim results: revenue RMB 87.5bn (+8.0% y/y), gross profit RMB 27.5bn (+32.3%), profit for the period RMB 19.1bn (+41.0%), net profit attributable RMB 17.2bn (+39.2%), basic EPS RMB 1.734 (+32.0%).
earnings.readthrough: THE READ-THROUGH IS ABOUT COST, NOT PROFIT. Gross profit rose 32.3% on revenue up only 8.0% because cost of sales DECLINED outright - the cleanest public confirmation this reporting season that the alumina price collapse has reached the integrated Chinese cost curve. For the metal itself this cuts both ways and the bearish leg deserves equal billing: the world's largest producer earning record margins at $3,200-3,300/t has no economic reason to restrain output, and a lower cost curve lowers the price floor at which supply discipline would ever appear. Public disclosure only; no company-specific or confidential information is used or implied.

earnings.headline: SWUNG BACK TO PROFIT ON THE PRICE CYCLE, WITH TEXTBOOK OPERATING LEVERAGE. Unaudited H1-2026 interim results, approved at an 18-August board meeting and filed 19-August: ADJUSTED EBITDA UP 64.4% TO US$1.23bn from US$748m; revenue up 10.9% to US$8.338bn from US$7.52bn; adjusted net profit US$196m against a US$194m loss a year earlier. Total sales cost rose 3.3% to US$6.31bn, attributed to higher energy costs.
earnings.readthrough: REVENUE UP A TENTH AGAINST EBITDA UP NEARLY TWO-THIRDS IS THE SAME OPERATING-LEVERAGE SIGNATURE EVERY OTHER PRODUCER ON THIS PANEL HAS REPORTED FOR THE FIRST HALF, and it confirms the pattern extends beyond Western and Gulf smelters. The cost line is the part worth noting rather than the profit line: sales cost rose only 3.3% while revenue rose 10.9%, so the margin expansion came from price rather than from cost deflation, and the company specifically attributed what cost inflation there was to ENERGY. That is consistent with the power and carbon risk carried on the input basket. The half captured aluminium reaching four-year highs before the retreat now visible on this board, so it is a backward-looking confirmation of the cycle rather than a forward signal.

earnings.headline: Revenue RMB 11.53bn, up 32.4% year on year. Net profit attributable to owners RMB 2.30bn, up 166.1%. EPS RMB 1.11 against RMB 0.58 in the corresponding period of last year, up 91.4%.
earnings.readthrough: THE CLEANEST PUBLIC READ THIS WEEK ON HOW FAR SMELTER MARGIN HAS EXPANDED AT 2026 PRICES, AND IT COMES FROM AN INTEGRATED, SELF-SUPPLIED PRODUCER. The company operates 788,100 t/y of electrolytic aluminium capacity in Huolinguole, Inner Mongolia with a captive power plant, plus an alumina refining and aluminium hydroxide base in Binzhou, Shandong; it states that self-sufficiency in alumina and electricity fully meets its production requirements. Profit attributable rose 166% on revenue up 32%, which is operating leverage of roughly five times and is only possible when the price rises against a cost base that does not. Management attributes the gain to higher electrolytic aluminium selling prices, lower production cost from a rising green-energy share, and an optimised financing structure. TWO FORWARD DISCLOSURES MATTER BEYOND the quarter: 1,040 MW of wind and 110 MW of solar were commissioned by end-June with the programme roughly 66% complete and the green share expected to exceed 50%, which lowers the cost base further; and the 500,000 t/y integrated electrolytic aluminium project in Saudi Arabia, invested with partners in 2025, had completed all compliance approvals with on-site construction in full swing. That project is a dated, sourced addition to the non-Chinese capacity pipeline. THE UNCOMFORTABLE IMPLICATION FOR PRICE BULLS: margins this wide at the low end of the cost curve are exactly the condition that funds new capacity, and this disclosure shows the funding and the capacity in the same document.

earnings.headline: MARGINS EXPANDED SHARPLY WITH A THIRD OF THE VOLUME GONE. Adjusted net profit Dh2.46bn, up 34% year-on-year. Adjusted EBITDA Dh4.51bn, up 11% from Dh4.07bn, with the adjusted EBITDA margin widening to 33.3% from 27.0%. Revenue FELL 10% to Dh13.54bn from Dh15.08bn as aluminium sales dropped 32% to 939,000 t and cast metal production fell 29% to 1.01 Mt following the March incident at Al Taweelah. Reported net income Dh1.74bn after a Dh725m net incident impact. The company estimates around Dh1.5bn of capital expenditure to restore Al Taweelah, most of it in 2026, and guided cast metal back to pre-incident levels in Q1-2027 with the smelter at 25% of its reduction cells as of 26-Aug-2026 (315 of 1,262).
earnings.readthrough: THE COMPOSITION IS A PUBLIC CONFIRMATION OF THE MARGIN STRUCTURE THIS BOARD HAS DESCRIBED ALL CYCLE. Profit rose on three named drivers - higher realised aluminium prices, stronger regional premiums and LOWER ALUMINA PRICES - while a third of the sales volume was simply unavailable. A 630 basis-point margin expansion on a 10% revenue decline is only possible when the cost side has fallen faster than the top line, and the alumina leg is the reason. IT ALSO EXPLAINS TODAY'S PRICE ACTION IN ONE LINE: the same release that showed the margin also showed the recovery date, and the market traded the recovery date. The read-across to the alumina panel is direct - if Alunorte's 50% rate ends up lifting seaborne alumina, this is the margin that compresses first across the Gulf fleet.

earnings.headline: RECORD QUARTER ACROSS EVERY SEGMENT. Consolidated revenue RS 84,825cr, up 32% year-on-year; consolidated EBITDA RS 14,989cr, up 73%; net profit RS 7,013cr, up 75%. The EBITDA margin printed 16.42% against 12.31% in Q1 FY26 and 12.82% in Q4 FY26 - a 411 basis-point expansion year-on-year and 360 basis points sequentially. INDIA ALUMINIUM UPSTREAM delivered its highest-ever quarterly EBITDA at RS 7,390cr, up 81%, comfortably exceeding the prior record of RS 5,448cr set in Q4 FY26. The COPPER segment also set a record at RS 918cr, up 36%. NOVELIS, the downstream subsidiary, reported adjusted EBITDA of $516m, up 24% from $416m a year earlier and equivalent to RS 4,875cr (+37%), with net income of $164m (+71%) and adjusted EBITDA of roughly $563 per tonne, helped by the restart of the Oswego hot mill in early June 2026 and continued Bay Minette commissioning.
earnings.readthrough: THIS IS THE CLEANEST PUBLIC EVIDENCE AVAILABLE OF HOW AN INTEGRATED PRODUCER CONVERTS THE 2026 PRICE STRUCTURE INTO MARGIN, AND THE CONVERSION RATE IS VERY HIGH. Revenue rose 32% while EBITDA rose 73% and upstream aluminium EBITDA rose 81% - operating leverage of well over two times on the upstream leg. The mechanism is integration: captive bauxite, captive alumina and captive coal-fired power insulate the cost stack from exactly the two legs that are currently rising for non-integrated smelters, namely seaborne bauxite (SMM index $71.57/mt, +$0.70 w/w) and seaborne alumina ($356/mt FOB East Australia on the 05-Aug trade). THE CONTRAST WITH CENTURY IS THE POINT. Century Aluminum, which buys its alumina, has now cited unfavourable raw-material price realisation as its principal EBITDA headwind for two consecutive quarters; Hindalco, which makes its own, posted a record. Management had guided to roughly 5% sequential aluminium cost inflation into this quarter and still delivered a record, which says the LME move more than absorbed it. FOR THE MARKET VIEW: this is bullish for the margin narrative and neutral-to-bearish for the supply narrative, because producers earning at this level have every incentive to run flat out and to accelerate the restart pipeline.

earnings.headline: Q2-2026 BEAT AND A HIGHER Q3 GUIDE: adjusted EBITDA attributable $326.9m against $315-335m guidance and $231.4m in Q1; net sales $752.1m (Q1 $649.2m); shipments 130,632 t (Q1 122,865 t); net income attributable $249.3m; diluted EPS $2.39; adjusted EPS $2.46. Q3-2026 guidance $325-345m. Liquidity $784.9m with cash $343.4m; cash exceeded total debt as of end-July after a $94.3m 2025 45X refund was received. Q2 adjustments included $61.3m for an Iceland equipment failure (net of tax) and $10.7m of Mt. Holly expansion cost.
earnings.readthrough: THE PUREST US AND SECTION-232 READ IN THE PEER SET, AND IT CONFIRMS THAT THE 2026 PRICE AND TARIFF STRUCTURE IS CONVERTING TO CASH. Adjusted EBITDA rose 41% sequentially on a 6.3% increase in shipments, which is operating leverage on price and premium rather than on volume. The last 90 Mt. Holly pots have been restarted, taking the plant to full capacity for the first time since 2015, and Grundartangi Line 2 is near full - so the volume base steps up again into Q3, which is why the guide moved higher despite Q2 already beating. THE COST-SIDE SIGNAL MATTERS FOR THE WHOLE BOARD: management again cited UNFAVOURABLE RAW-MATERIAL PRICE REALISATION as the principal EBITDA headwind, the second consecutive quarter it has done so. That is the same message the input basket carries - a firming alumina and bauxite leg partly offsetting a falling energy leg - and it is the reason a rising LME does not translate one-for-one into producer margin.

earnings.headline: BACK-FILLED INTO THE PER-COMPANY HISTORY PANEL THIS RUN WITH FOUR SOURCED QUARTERS OF ADJUSTED EBITDA. Q1 FY27 (three months to 30-June-2026): net income $164m, up 71% year on year; ADJUSTED EBITDA $516m, UP 24% year on year; adjusted EBITDA per tonne shipped $563, up 30% year on year; net sales $5.8bn. The prior three quarters were $459m in Q4 FY26 (down 3% y/y, $544/t), $348m in Q3 FY26 (down 5% y/y, $430/t) and $422m in Q2 FY26 (down 9% y/y, $448/t) - all three depressed by the Oswego fires of September and November 2025 and by tariff headwinds.
earnings.readthrough: THE FOUR-QUARTER SERIES IS THE POINT AND IT IS WHY THIS COMPANY WAS CHOSEN FOR THIS RUN'S BACKFILL: it is the cleanest public evidence available of how a downstream converter recovers from an operational shock, and of what the 2026 premium environment has been worth to the downstream. Adjusted EBITDA fell for three consecutive quarters - $422m, $348m, $459m - and then stepped up 12.4% sequentially and 24% year on year to $516m in the June quarter. THE PER-TONNE LINE IS THE MORE INFORMATIVE OF THE TWO because it strips shipment volume out: $448, $430, $544, $563. That is a 31% improvement in unit conversion economics across four quarters in a business whose metal cost is passed through. WHAT IT DOES NOT PROVE IS AS IMPORTANT AS WHAT IT DOES: a converter's EBITDA per tonne rising through a period of record US premiums is consistent with the premium being captured downstream, but Novelis does not publish a split between recovered metal-price spread, recycling spread and true conversion pricing, so this page does not claim one. THE GENERIC READ-ACROSS IS THAT THE DOWNSTREAM SIDE OF THE CHAIN ENTERED THE SECOND HALF OF 2026 WITH MOMENTUM, which is consistent with Constellium and Kaiser on the same panel and with the stable $727.50 Rotterdam billet conversion spread on the premium panel.

earnings.headline: Q2-2026 profit attributable to equity holders BHD 64.9m (US$172.5m), +164% y/y; Q2 EBITDA US$295m; EPS 46 fils. H1 profit BHD 140.2m (US$372.8m), +228% y/y; EPS 99 fils. OPERATIONALLY THE WEAKEST PRINT IN THE PEER SET: Q2 net finished production 155,469 t, DOWN 61% y/y, and sales volume 280,799 t, -32% y/y, with Lines 1, 2 and 3 still under controlled shutdown on regional tensions and raw-material availability. Value-added product was 195,891 t, 70% of shipments.
earnings.readthrough: THE SHARPEST ILLUSTRATION ON THIS BOARD OF WHAT THE 2026 MARKET IS ACTUALLY REWARDING: a producer can lose 61% of its output year-on-year and still nearly triple half-year profit, because average LME rose 46% y/y to $3,576/t in Q2. It also quantifies the supply loss the deficit rests on - Alba's own read put the Q2 global deficit at 934,000 t including China and 626,000 t excluding it, with global supply contracting about 1% mainly on Middle East disruption. Management explicitly framed the curtailments as preserving flexibility for a swift recovery when conditions improve, which is the restart option the bearish case depends on. Separately Alba is progressing its US$2.2bn acquisition of Aluminium Dunkerque, about 300,000 t/y and the largest EU smelter.

earnings.headline: Q3-2026: revenue $3.704bn (-7% q/q from $3.966bn); net income attributable $483m, $1.81/share; ADJUSTED EPS $1.82 against $2.12 in Q2 - a BEAT against the ~$1.54 consensus cited by Investing.com while revenue missed (~$3.78bn expected). Adjusted EBITDA excluding special items $789m (Q2 $901m). Alumina production +11% to 2.467 Mt (Pinjarra stability); aluminium production +2% to 649 kt (Alumar restart complete); total aluminium shipments -5% to 693 kt. Realised aluminium $4,527/t (Q2 $4,752/t); third-party alumina $353/t (Q2 $334/t). FY2026 production and shipment guidance reaffirmed.
earnings.readthrough: THE FIRST Q3 PRODUCER PRINT SHOWS THE PEAK IS BEHIND THE AVERAGE REALISED PRICE: a ~5% q/q fall in realised aluminium and a 7% revenue drop, offset by better costs and a higher alumina price. Q4 guidance flags about $30m of higher raw-material costs and maintenance in the aluminium segment and about $30m higher alumina costs - consistent with an industry where the metal price is easing faster than input costs. The South32 aluminium chain acquisition (shareholder-approved 15-October) is guided to close in H1-2027. Generic public read-through, not advice.

earnings.headline: Q3-2026: adjusted EBITDA NOK 9,089m against NOK 8,923m in Q2 and NOK 5,996m in Q3-2025; Aluminium Metal adjusted EBITDA NOK 7,031m (Q3-2025 NOK 2,732m); Bauxite & Alumina NOK 283m (from NOK 1,290m); Energy NOK 411m (from NOK 828m). Free cash flow NOK 1.4bn, reduced by higher working capital tied to higher metal prices; adjusted net debt NOK 21.9bn (NOK 22.8bn last quarter). Capex guidance cut to about NOK 12.5bn from NOK 13.5bn; Slovalco's first restart phase targets 75,000 t/y by end-February 2027. Shares fell about 7% on the day (Investing.com).
earnings.readthrough: THE SMELTER LEG IS STILL EARNING ON PRICE, THE ALUMINA LEG IS NOT. Aluminium Metal EBITDA more than doubled year on year on higher all-in metal prices despite lower volumes and higher energy and carbon costs, while Bauxite & Alumina fell nearly 80% on lower alumina prices, LNG sourcing costs at Alunorte (about $85m in Q3, $90-110m guided for Q4 per management) and BRL effects. Hydro describes the ex-China alumina market as oversupplied and ex-China primary demand as declining, with Middle East tension keeping aluminium prices elevated - the same split as Alcoa's Q3: metal margin intact, alumina margin compressing, cash absorbed by working capital.

earnings.headline: Net profit RS 5,629cr, +216% YoY (consolidated PAT reported at RS 6,597cr, +205%, on some feeds - consolidation basis differs); revenue RS 21,393cr (+46% YoY); EBITDA RS 10,299cr vs RS 8,352cr in Q4 FY26 (+23% q/q), margin 48.1% vs 43.7%; interim dividend RS 8/share; record output 632 kt (+5% y/y) with record value-added 389 kt (+14%).
earnings.readthrough: The cleanest India read on the 2026 regime: a low-cost integrated producer converting the price/premium environment into a near-50% EBITDA margin, with volume records on top. Confirms the pattern set by Alcoa, Hydro, Rio and South32 - the Hormuz-era price structure is flowing straight through to producer P&Ls, and value-added mix is expanding, not shrinking, into the squeeze.

earnings.headline: Net profit $200.3m (+316% YoY); EPS 53 fils; sales −17% on Gulf supply-chain disruption.
earnings.readthrough: LME averaged $3,195/t (+22% YoY) drove profit surge; volumes hit by regional conflict; ~19% capacity in controlled shutdown — restart path improves post-truce.

earnings.headline: Net profit SAR 2.18bn (+13% y/y, +33% q/q); revenue SAR 10.9bn (+16% y/y, +24% q/q); gross profit SAR 3.39bn (-4%) and operating profit SAR 2.36bn (-8%).
earnings.readthrough: A clean example of the split running through this whole peer season: the top line and the bottom line rose on higher commodity prices across all business units and higher aluminium and gold sales volumes, while GROSS and OPERATING profit FELL on input and logistics cost inflation - here concentrated in phosphate (sulphur, freight) rather than in the aluminium chain. Net profit was additionally helped by higher finance income, lower finance costs and a larger share of equity-accounted profits, so the headline overstates the operating improvement. The generic read for the aluminium market is the same one Century and Hindalco delivered from opposite ends of the integration spectrum: a rising metal price is not converting one-for-one into margin wherever the input leg is bought rather than owned.

earnings.headline: Group revenue $31.0bn (+15%); underlying EBITDA $14.8bn (+28%); free cash flow +75%; dividend raised. ALUMINIUM segment EBITDA +31%. Primary aluminium 1,676 kt (flat), alumina 4,040 kt (+8%), bauxite 28.5 Mt (-7%).
earnings.readthrough: UPDATE 17-OCTOBER (Q3-2026 operations review, 14-October, production only - no new earnings figures): primary aluminium 842 kt (-2% y/y), alumina 2,071 kt (+10% y/y), 2026 aluminium guidance 3.25-3.45 Mt unchanged; average Midwest duty-paid premium $2,420/t on about 32% of Q3 volumes. earnings.readthrough: THE READ-THROUGH IS A WARNING ABOUT HOW MUCH OF THE 2026 DOWNSTREAM EARNINGS CYCLE IS A PRICE ARTEFACT RATHER THAN A DEMAND ONE, AND KAISER DISCLOSES IT MORE HONESTLY THAN MOST. Adjusted EBITDA includes management-estimated FAVOURABLE METAL PRICE LAG of approximately $27.0m in Q2-2026 and $36.0m in Q1-2026 - $64.0m across the half against $36.0m in H1-2025. That is roughly 22% of H1-2026 adjusted EBITDA arising from the timing difference between the Midwest Transaction Price embedded in cost of sales and the market price over the period, not from conversion economics. MANAGEMENT SAID SO EXPLICITLY: the raised full-year outlook 'assumes a NEUTRAL metal price lag through the end of the year, and does not assume a continuation of the metal lag or consumption cost tailwinds recorded in the first half', and the CEO said the company expects aluminium price dynamics to normalise over the balance of the year. THE COMMERCIAL LESSON FOR READING THIS WHOLE PANEL: a rising aluminium price inflates downstream converter earnings twice - once through genuine mix and volume, once through inventory timing - and the second half reverses if the price stops rising. Kaiser's underlying story is nevertheless real: conversion revenue per pound rose to $1.43 from $1.30, packaging conversion revenue per pound rose to $1.12 from $0.92, and aerospace shipments grew as destocking eased. Both things are true at once and the filing quantifies the split, which is why this row is worth its place.

Deficit - Goldman -720 kt, Norsk Hydro -900 kt, Macquarie -930 kt; Citi an outlier at -2.7 Mt. THE BALANCE VIEW IS UNCHANGED AND THE 11-SEPTEMBER DATA SHARPENS THE CENTRAL PUZZLE RATHER THAN RESOLVING IT: global primary production was reported down 1.7% year on year at 6.16 million tonnes and GCC output down 44% year on year in July to 293,000 tonnes from 523,000 - a genuine, large supply loss. YET China's August exports were 626,000 tonnes, taking January-August to 4.67 million tonnes, up 16.7% year on year, and dated commentary describes Middle Eastern and Australian ingot supply into Japan as RELATIVELY AMPLE with Asian premiums collapsing toward a $280-290 Q4 consensus. A DEFICIT IN PRIMARY UNITS CAN COEXIST WITH AMPLE REGIONAL AVAILABILITY IF THE RELIEVING METAL ARRIVES AS CHINESE SEMI-FINISHED AND ALLOY PRODUCT THAT NEVER PASSES THROUGH AN LME WAREHOUSE - which is the most coherent published explanation for why a multi-decade exchange inventory low, a widening backwardation and collapsing physical premiums are all true at once.

The published restart schedule is the reason, and it gained another dated entry on 20-August. Nanshan Aluminum's 2026 semi-annual report confirms 250,000 t/y of Indonesian aluminium and 260,000 t/y of carbon under construction at Bintan Industrial Park, with the integrated anode carbon removing one of the genuine physical constraints on commissioning new non-Chinese capacity. Alongside it: Gulf pre-incident output guided for Q1-2027 and running faster than the market expected; Slovalco 75,000 t/y from Q4-2026; Magnitude 7 Metals 75,000 t/y before year-end; Mount Holly already at full capacity and lifting US primary output by close to 10%; the Australian smelter's power secured to 2038 removing a closure risk over up to 590,000 t/y; Alunorte back at full rate; and a 500,000 t/y integrated Saudi greenfield through all compliance approvals with construction under way. These are published commitments with dates attached rather than projections, which is why the deficit is expected to narrow rather than persist at 2026 scale.

premium_explainer: PREMIUMS ARE WHAT A BUYER PAYS OVER THE EXCHANGE PRICE TO GET PHYSICAL METAL DELIVERED TO A PARTICULAR PLACE, AND THEY ARE THE PART OF THE DELIVERED PRICE THAT THE EXCHANGE DOES NOT SET. They are assessed by price-reporting agencies from reported transactions on defined periodic cycles - quarterly for the Japanese benchmark, weekly or twice-weekly for most spot assessments - which is why this panel carries each row at its own assessment date instead of pretending to a daily figure. Each row is carried at its own last public assessment date; the CIF Japan spot row uses SMM's 09-October mark. THREE THINGS DRIVE A PREMIUM: the cost of physically moving and financing metal to that location; how hard it is to get metal there right now; and policy - duties, tariffs and carbon costs that apply at the border. THE POLICY COMPONENT IS THE ONLY ONE THAT CAN BE CALCULATED RATHER THAN ASSESSED, AND THIS PAGE CALCULATES IT SEPARATELY SO THE TWO ARE NEVER CONFUSED. At a verified 50% Section 232 rate on full customs value, the tariff leg of the US duty-paid premium is $1,627.00 against cash of $3,254.00, which is 67.7% of the $2,403/t US duty-paid premium. The remaining $776.00 is the market leg. When cash moves, the tariff leg moves with it mechanically and the market leg absorbs the difference - today cash rose $26.00, the tariff leg rose $13.00 and the market leg fell $13.00 without any physical market having changed. THE EXCHANGE CURVE IS THE CLEANEST PUBLIC READ ON THE IMMEDIACY COMPONENT, AND IT IMPROVED FOR THE SELLER TODAY. A contango means the market charges to defer metal, which weakens a physical premium; a backwardation means it pays for metal now, which strengthens one. The contango narrowed $11.50 to $13.00 from $24.50 on the 25-September official, so the buyer's structural argument going into the Q4 Japanese settlement is weaker this morning than it was on the prior session.

A buyer arguing for a deep cut leans on a curve that charges to defer metal; that argument is close to half as strong this morning as it was on the prior session. WHAT STILL FAVOURS THE BUYER: the last public Chinese spot review, dated 24-September, records metal clearing at repeated discounts with quotes lowered through the session; ex-China operating capacity is publicly recovering, with Alba's restart the largest single tranche in the public record this cycle and Century, Slovalco and Magnitude 7 all guided; European gas fell 4.02% on the 25-September reference session, improving the economics of the European capacity guided to return; and Friday's Chinese customs data show August primary imports down 14.65% year on year, which means less Chinese competition for ex-China units. alumina_explainer: ALUMINA IS THE FEEDSTOCK: it takes roughly two tonnes of alumina to make one tonne of aluminium, so the alumina price is the single largest raw-material line in a smelter's cost stack - about 34% of Chinese full cost on public estimates. A smelter's margin is therefore driven as much by what alumina costs as by what aluminium sells for.

THE RATIO MATTERS MORE THAN THE LEVEL. Alumina at $363.60/t against an aluminium three-month of $3,267.00 is a ratio of 11.13%, against a decade norm of 15-17%. Alumina is therefore still historically CHEAP relative to metal. The ratio fell from 11.18% on the prior session and the reason is worth stating precisely: the metal rose 0.45% and no alumina price changed. When a ratio moves because its denominator moved, that is a margin event for smelters, not an alumina event.

THE DIVERGENCE THIS PAGE HAS TRACKED FOR SEVERAL RUNS IS UNCHANGED AND STILL THE MOST USEFUL THING IN THIS PANEL: Chinese alumina has been drifting sideways to lower while ex-China alumina has been firmer. The SMM index at 2,671.59 yuan/tonne for 24-September is essentially flat, and FOB East Australia at $354.00/t for 18-September sits well above the Q2-2026 average of $307.40/t. Two independent series, one Chinese and one seaborne, pointing different ways is a stronger observation than either alone.

THE CAUSE IS LOGISTICS RATHER THAN A SHORTAGE OF REFINING CAPACITY, WHICH IS WHY IT SITS ALONGSIDE THE HORMUZ ROW. The ex-China firmness has been publicly attributed to Middle East transport problems lifting demand for bagged alumina and for alternative origins, not to any shortfall in installed refining capacity.

SUPPLY ITSELF IS NOT THE CONSTRAINT AND THAT IS STATED SO THE DIVERGENCE IS NOT OVER-READ. China's national weekly alumina operating rate is 76.89% on 119.62 Mt/y of capacity, so there is very substantial idle refining capacity available to respond to any sustained price signal. A seaborne market that is firm because of shipping frictions, sitting on top of a refining industry running at roughly three-quarters of capacity, is not a structural alumina shortage.

WHAT TO WATCH: whether the Chinese index resumes falling while the seaborne price holds. If it does, ex-China smelters keep a cost advantage relative to Chinese peers that is unusual in this cycle; if the Chinese index turns up, the cheapest leg of the global cost curve rises and the margin story narrows for everybody. SMM publishes the index weekly on Thursdays, so the next print is due 01-October.

premium_drivers.t: The Q4 Japanese premium has settled 35% lower, at $255/t
premium_drivers.d: SETTLED: Reuters (07-October) reported that some Japanese buyers agreed to pay $255/t over LME cash for October-December shipments, down 35% from $395/t in Q3 and below producers' initial offers of $310-325/t; producers named in the talks included Rio Tinto and South32, and talks with other buyers were ongoing. A Japanese trading-house source cited recovering Middle East output after the March attacks on Gulf smelters and rising Indonesian shipments. Negotiations ran longer than usual because of a wide gap between the two sides. The settlement sits inside the $245-260/t offer range AL Circle reported on 06-October, and above CRU's $202/t Asia CIF assessment. WHY IT MATTERS: the quarterly MJP is the reference for much Asian physical business, so the regional premium level resets about $140/t lower for the quarter.

premium_drivers.t: Chinese primary imports fell 14.65% year on year in August, which means less Chinese competition for ex-China metal
premium_drivers.d: Public customs data reported on 25-September show China's August primary aluminium imports at 185,500 tonnes, DOWN 14.65% year on year and up just 0.16% month on month, with Russia supplying 178,150 tonnes or 96% of the total and Australia (2,920 t), Indonesia (2,180 t) and Malaysia (1,800 t) accounting for almost all of the remainder. Net imports were 163,600 tonnes, down 14.67% year on year. January-August imports were 1.66 million tonnes, down 3.41%. THE STATED CAUSE IS STRUCTURAL RATHER THAN DEMAND-LED: domestic capacity is at the 45-million-tonne policy ceiling, end-use demand from grid investment, electric vehicles and photovoltaic mounting is described as resilient, and inventory is being drawn down through semis exports rather than primary imports. WHY IT MATTERS FOR PREMIUMS EVEN SO: a premium is set by competition for units at a location. China importing 14.65% less primary metal, and 96% of what it does import arriving from a single discounted-origin supplier, means the marginal ex-China unit faces less Chinese competition - which works against premiums in Japan, Europe and the United States regardless of why Chinese buying fell.
src: AL Circle - China Aug aluminium imports down 14.7% year on year, Russia accounts for 96% of supply (25-September-2026)

premium_drivers.t: Chinese semis exports hit a 2026 high, which pressures converter margins in exactly the markets where premiums are assessed
premium_drivers.d: Public data reported on 25-September show China's August aluminium extrusion exports at 92,500 tonnes, the highest monthly figure of 2026, up 9.7% year on year from 84,300 tonnes and 3.0% month on month from 89,800 tonnes, taking January-August to 629,600 tonnes, up 8.7%. South-East Asia took 26,500 tonnes or 28.6% and was the only region with both the largest volume and double-digit growth; Africa took 18,800 tonnes and Latin America 14,400. SEPTEMBER IS GUIDED LOWER at 85,000-92,000 tonnes because the China-to-overseas price spread has narrowed, compressing margins on independent order-taking; the share of processing trade rose while ordinary trade fell, which the source reads as marginal weakening in price-driven independent orders. THE PREMIUM READ IS SPECIFIC: extrusions compete with locally converted metal in third markets. More Chinese semis arriving in South-East Asia, Africa and Latin America pressures the converter margins that ultimately support regional ingot premiums, even though the same exports support Chinese domestic ingot demand. The two effects are opposite and are stated separately rather than netted.

UPDATED 22-OCTOBER (SMM, 22-October): Chinese aluminium ingot social inventory fell 53,000 t in the second week after National Day, 103,000 t over two weeks - the fastest post-holiday pace since at least 2020; billets -20,000 t. Public commentary (Kedia Advisory, 29-September) cites China's August output at a record 3.98 million tonnes. UPDATED 30-SEPTEMBER: SMM reports aluminium ingot inventory at 638,000 t, down 36,000 t from Monday, with A00 spot at 24,110 yuan/t and limited pre-holiday downstream stocking; SHFE closes 01-08 October for National Day. UPDATED 28-SEPTEMBER WITH SMM'S LAST PRE-HOLIDAY INVENTORY PRINT: ingot 674,000 t (-4,000 t vs Thursday), 6063 billet 154,500 t (+5,500 t vs Thursday). REVIEWED 28-SEPTEMBER (LAST REFRESHED 27-SEPTEMBER) WITH GENUINELY NEW PUBLIC TRADE DATA, AND IT CUTS AGAINST THE EX-CHINA TIGHTNESS CASE FROM BOTH ENDS. Customs data reported 25-September show China's AUGUST PRIMARY ALUMINIUM IMPORTS DOWN 14.65% YEAR ON YEAR AT 185,500 TONNES, with Russia supplying 178,150 tonnes or 96% of the total; net imports 163,600 tonnes, down 14.67% year on year; January-August imports 1.66 million tonnes, down 3.41%. ON THE SAME DAY, AUGUST ALUMINIUM EXTRUSION EXPORTS PRINTED A 2026 HIGH OF 92,500 TONNES, up 9.7% year on year and 3.0% month on month, taking January-August to 629,600 tonnes, up 8.7%; September is guided lower at 85,000-92,000 tonnes on a narrowing China-to-overseas price spread. THE STATED CAUSE OF THE IMPORT FALL IS STRUCTURAL RATHER THAN DEMAND-LED - domestic capacity at the 45-million-tonne policy ceiling, resilient end-use demand from grid investment, electric vehicles and photovoltaic mounting, and inventory drawn down through semis exports rather than primary imports. WHY IT MATTERS FOR THIS ROW SPECIFICALLY: the 45 Mt ceiling is the load-bearing assumption of the structural-deficit case, and these two prints are the first public evidence in this window of how China is behaving AT the ceiling - importing less primary and exporting more semis. Both work against ex-China tightness whatever the cause. The August record-output figures carried in the status line are unchanged and no newer output print landed in this window.

FIRST, THE INBOUND CORRIDOR: China's August primary aluminium imports fell 14.65% year on year to 185,500 tonnes, with Russia supplying 178,150 tonnes or 96% of the total and Australia, Indonesia and Malaysia accounting for almost all of the rest. January-August imports were 1.66 million tonnes, down 3.41%. A single origin at 96% is a concentration worth recording in its own right, and a 14.65% fall means less Chinese competition for ex-China units. SECOND, THE OUTBOUND SEMIS CORRIDOR: August extrusion exports hit a 2026 high of 92,500 tonnes, up 9.7% year on year, with South-East Asia at 26,500 tonnes or 28.6%, Africa at 18,800 and Latin America at 14,400 - and September guided lower at 85,000-92,000 tonnes on a narrowing China-to-overseas price spread. THE HORMUZ AND RED SEA ROWS ARE UNCHANGED: nothing operational printed into this window, the 07-September negotiating track remains the last dated development, and nothing has been signed. The Canada-United States row is unchanged with the rate re-verified. The Indonesia row is unchanged. NOTHING HERE HAS BEEN ROLLED FORWARD AS IF NEW; each corridor carries its own last sourced development.

August aluminium extrusion exports printed a 2026 HIGH of 92,500 tonnes, up 9.7% year on year from 84,300 and 3.0% month on month from 89,800, taking January-August to 629,600 tonnes, up 8.7%. South-East Asia took 26,500 tonnes or 28.6% and was the only region with both the largest volume and double-digit growth; Africa took 18,800 tonnes and Latin America 14,400. SEPTEMBER IS GUIDED LOWER AT 85,000-92,000 TONNES because the China-to-overseas price spread has narrowed, compressing margins on independent order-taking; processing trade gained share while ordinary trade lost it, which the source reads as marginal weakening in price-driven independent orders. THE CORRIDOR READ: semi-finished exports remain the principal mechanism by which Chinese metal reaches shortage markets without primary metal crossing a border, and it is running at its 2026 peak. That relieves physical tightness in Western markets while pressuring Western fabricator margins - the same trade does both, and this page states both rather than netting them. The earlier January-June figure of 3.2 Mt of semis exports, up 18% year on year with June at a record 695,000 tonnes, is the wider context and is unchanged.

flows.impact: swing - and now measurably importing less primary while exporting more semis
flows.note: REVISED THIS RUN ON NEW PUBLIC CUSTOMS DATA. China's AUGUST PRIMARY ALUMINIUM IMPORTS fell 14.65% year on year to 185,500 tonnes, up just 0.16% month on month, with RUSSIA SUPPLYING 178,150 TONNES OR 96% of the total; Australia contributed 2,920 tonnes, Indonesia 2,180 and Malaysia 1,800. Net imports were 163,600 tonnes, down 14.67% year on year but up 6.44% month on month. January-August imports were 1.66 million tonnes, down 3.41% year on year; January-August net imports 1.49 Mt, down 4.65%. THE STATED CAUSE IS STRUCTURAL: domestic capacity at the 45-million-tonne policy ceiling, resilient end-use demand from power grid investment, electric vehicles and photovoltaic mounting structures, and inventory drawn down through extrusion exports rather than primary imports. The source is explicit that imports have not collapsed but maintained a steady inflow. THE CORRIDOR READ: China at the ceiling is importing less primary and exporting more semis, and 96% of what it does import comes from a single discounted-origin supplier. That combination reduces Chinese competition for ex-China primary units - which is a headwind for ex-China premiums and for the ex-China tightness case, whatever the cause. The earlier compositional point remains valid context: a high liquid-aluminium proportion means less deliverable ingot reaches the Chinese domestic market even at capped output.
